candidate.blueprint_locator: Basic Care and Comfort — nutrition and skin/wound care
candidate.blueprint_topic: Basic Care and Comfort — nutrition for pressure-injury healing
candidate.educational_objective: Explain that adequate individualized protein and overall nutrition support pressure-injury healing.

options.A: Protein should be restricted in every client with a pressure injury because protein delays tissue repair.
options.B: Nutritional intake is unrelated to pressure-injury healing once local wound care has started.
options.C: Vitamin supplements can replace adequate energy and protein intake for tissue repair in all clients.
options.D: Adequate protein and overall nutrition support tissue repair and wound healing; nutrition needs should be individualized to the client's condition.

candidate.rationale: Pressure-injury management includes nutritional assessment and adequate nutrient intake to support healing. Protein is important to tissue repair, but the plan should be individualized rather than applying a fixed amount or universal restriction. A through C contradict the role of nutrition in wound healing.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Pressure-injury care includes attention to adequate nutrition and protein for tissue repair/healing, individualized to the patient.
candidate.source_locator: Treatment/Management; Deterrence and Patient Education — nutritional assessment/support in pressure-injury care
candidate.source_organization: National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI Bookshelf)
candidate.stem: A client with a healing pressure injury asks why the dietitian emphasized adequate protein intake. Which explanation is best?
